top_entities.name: CenterPoint Energy
top_entities.news_summary: A threat actor claimed theft of a 7.49M-record CenterPoint Energy customer database (names, phone numbers, addresses, driver's license numbers, partial SSNs) beginning 1 September 2026 (outside this window). The materially new, in-window development is the legal and disclosure response: at least five proposed federal class-action lawsuits were filed against CenterPoint between 10-13 September 2026 (Shamis & Gentile; Lippe & Associates) on behalf of Texas, Indiana and Minnesota customers, and CenterPoint filed an SEC Form 8-K on 14 September 2026 confirming awareness of the breach claim. CenterPoint has not confirmed the 7.49M figure or dataset authenticity -- that specific figure rests partly on an undated source (cyberinsider.com) and should be treated as an unconfirmed claimant figure, not a verified fact, pending CenterPoint's own disclosure.

top_entities.name: Ukraine
top_entities.news_summary: A brief (5-8 September 2026) Ukraine-ordered ceasefire during a US-mediated visit by envoys Witkoff and Kushner ended when Russia launched a large-scale drone-and-missile attack on Kyiv overnight 8 September 2026, killing 5 and injuring 35, and damaging residential buildings, a school and warehouses. ATTRIBUTION NOTE for the assessor: this is Russian conduct directed AT Ukraine, not conduct BY the Ukrainian state -- analogous to the LAHSA/Los Angeles attribution question flagged in prior cycles. Any scoring should weigh Ukraine's own institutional response (civilian protection, humanitarian coordination) rather than treat the strike itself as Ukraine's conduct.

top_entities.name: Bangladesh
top_entities.news_summary: Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal sentenced seven former Awami League officials to death in absentia for crimes against humanity connected to the state's suppression of the 2024 student-led protests (at least 1,400 deaths, per the UN). Reported 15 September 2026 (per a 21 September weekly recap covering 14-20 September). Direction is ambiguous for scoring purposes: it is accountability for a prior atrocity (positive signal), but delivered via death sentences and in absentia (a due-process concern in its own right) -- flagged for the assessor to weigh rather than pre-judged here. Bangladesh's most recent assessment (2026-09-01) pre-dates this ruling.

Corroborates Iran's existing near-floor placement (composite 2.5, critical band) rather than indicating a change in direction.
